title: Adaptive ingress throttling and graceful fallback for reserved fleets
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive ingress throttling layer for Dedicated fleets that enforces per-customer throughput commitments, maintains tail-latency SLOs, and performs staged graceful degradation when capacity pressure is detected. The feature combines a lightweight per-tenant token-bucket with a fleet headroom signal, an observable ingress queue with position/ETA streaming, and a multi-phase shedding policy that prefers soft fallbacks (cached or lower-cost model variants) before hard request rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress applies per-tenant throughput caps that can be configured via fleet policies and are enforced under contention.

When fleet headroom falls below configured thresholds the system initiates a three-phase response: slow-path (queue/retry with ETA), fallback-path (served by cached prefixes or compatible cheaper model variant), then hard-shed (503 with Retry-After).
Autoscaler consumes queue and headroom metrics to proactively add capacity; empirical tests show 30% reduction in hard-shed events for synthetic load spikes in staging.
Telemetry dashboards expose shed-rate, fallback-rate, p95/p99 latency, queue length and average ETA per-tenant; alerts trigger when customer SLA burn > 1% per hour.
New feature toggles allow per-customer opt-out and gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% of Dedicated fleets via Console rollout policies.
notes: Design trade-offs: We avoid per-request heavyweight negotiation to keep p95 overhead < 2ms. Token-bucket parameters are tuned to align with committed throughput while allowing short bursts for transient bursts from warm-prefixes.

We choose a three-phase shedding strategy to maximize successful work: 1) queue and provide ETA stream for clients that can wait, 2) attempt fallback to cached prefix or quantized model variant (prefers quality-preserving fallbacks), 3) final hard rejection with machine-readable reason codes for client-side backoff and metrics.

Edge cases: cold cache + simultaneous fleet pressure requires conservative fallback thresholds to avoid cascading quality regressions. We'll instrument quality regression checks tied to prompt-set evals to monitor damage.
Rollout gating: enable only after runtime-1.18 kernel scheduling release and after the autoscaler exposes predicted queue_size metric (dependency ENG-14687).
